title: Pair With Target Sum
statement:
Given a list of integers `nums` and an integer `target`, return the indices `[i, j]` (with `i < j`) of the two numbers that add up to `target`.

Exactly one valid pair exists. You may not use the same element twice.

mentorNotes.keyInsight: For each number x, the only partner that works is target - x. Remember what you have seen in a hash map (value → index) so the check is O(1).
mentorNotes.bruteForce: Try every pair i < j: O(n²) time, O(1) space.
mentorNotes.optimal: One pass with a hash map: check whether target - x was seen before inserting x. O(n) time, O(n) space.
commonMistakes: Inserting x before checking, so [3,2,4] with target 6 pairs 3 with itself
Returning the values instead of the indices
Returning indices in the wrong order

title: Duplicate Finder
statement: Given a list of integers `nums`, return `true` if any value appears at least twice, and `false` if every value is distinct.

mentorNotes.keyInsight: You only need to know whether you've seen a value before, so a set answers that in O(1).
mentorNotes.bruteForce: Compare every pair: O(n²).
mentorNotes.optimal: Sort and compare neighbours (O(n log n)), or a hash set (O(n) time, O(n) space).
commonMistakes: Comparing adjacent elements without sorting first

title: Anagram Check
statement: Given two strings `s` and `t` of lowercase letters, return `true` if `t` uses exactly the same letters as `s`, the same number of times each (in any order).

mentorNotes.keyInsight: Two strings are anagrams exactly when every letter has the same count in both.
mentorNotes.bruteForce: Sort both strings and compare: O(n log n).
mentorNotes.optimal: Count letters with a 26-slot array or hash map: O(n) time, O(1) extra space.
commonMistakes: Comparing sets, which ignores counts (aab vs abb)
Forgetting the length check

title: Most Frequent K
statement:
Given a list of integers `nums` and an integer `k`, return the `k` most frequent values.

Order the result from most to least frequent. If two values are equally frequent, the smaller value comes first.

mentorNotes.keyInsight: First count every value; then the question becomes ordering values by count. Buckets indexed by count avoid a full sort.
mentorNotes.bruteForce: Count, then sort all distinct values by (-count, value): O(n log n).
mentorNotes.optimal: Bucket sort by frequency: O(n). A heap of size k gives O(n log k).
commonMistakes: Ignoring the tie-break rule
Returning counts instead of values
edgeCases: k equals the number of distinct values

title: Clean Palindrome
statement: Given a string `s`, return `true` if it reads the same forwards and backwards after ignoring uppercase/lowercase differences and skipping every character that is not a letter or digit.

mentorNotes.keyInsight: Compare from both ends inward, skipping characters that don't count; no need to build a cleaned copy.
mentorNotes.bruteForce: Build a cleaned lowercase string and compare it with its reverse: O(n) time, O(n) space.
mentorNotes.optimal: Two pointers from both ends, skipping non-alphanumerics: O(n) time, O(1) space.
commonMistakes: Forgetting digits count as alphanumeric
Not lowercasing
Pointers crossing without a check

title: Pair Sum, Sorted
statement:
`nums` is sorted in non-decreasing order. Return the indices `[i, j]` (with `i < j`) of the two numbers that add up to `target`.

Exactly one valid pair exists. Try to use O(1) extra space.

mentorNotes.keyInsight: Because the list is sorted, if the current sum is too small only moving the left pointer right can help; if too big, only moving the right pointer left can.
mentorNotes.bruteForce: All pairs O(n²), or a hash map O(n) time with O(n) space.
mentorNotes.optimal: Two pointers at both ends moving inward: O(n) time, O(1) space.
commonMistakes: Moving the wrong pointer
Ignoring that the input is sorted

title: Zero-Sum Triplets
statement:
Given a list of integers `nums`, return every unique triplet of values `[a, b, c]` taken from three different positions such that `a + b + c == 0`.

Write each triplet in ascending order (`a ≤ b ≤ c`). No triplet may appear twice. The triplets themselves can be in any order.

mentorNotes.keyInsight: Sort first. Fix one value, then the remaining two form a sorted pair-sum problem solved with two pointers. Sorting also makes skipping duplicates easy.
mentorNotes.bruteForce: Try every triple and deduplicate with a set: O(n³).
mentorNotes.optimal: Sort, then for each i run two pointers on the rest, skipping repeated values: O(n²) time.
commonMistakes: Returning duplicate triplets
Skipping duplicates before using the first occurrence
Not sorting each triplet

title: Widest Water Tank
statement:
`heights[i]` is the height of a vertical wall at position `i`. Pick two walls; together with the ground they hold water up to the height of the shorter wall.

Return the largest amount of water any pair can hold: `min(heights[i], heights[j]) * (j - i)`.

mentorNotes.keyInsight: Start with the widest pair. The shorter wall limits the area, so moving the taller wall inward can never help; always move the shorter one.
mentorNotes.bruteForce: Check every pair: O(n²).
mentorNotes.optimal: Two pointers from both ends, moving the shorter wall: O(n).
commonMistakes: Moving the taller wall
Using the taller wall's height in the area

title: Max Sum Window of K
statement: Given a list of integers `nums` and an integer `k`, return the largest sum of any `k` consecutive elements.

mentorNotes.keyInsight: Neighbouring windows share k-1 elements. Add the one that enters and subtract the one that leaves instead of re-summing.
mentorNotes.bruteForce: Sum every window from scratch: O(n·k).
mentorNotes.optimal: Keep a running window sum: O(n) time, O(1) space.
commonMistakes: Starting best at 0 when all numbers are negative
Off-by-one when removing the leaving element

title: Longest Unique Stretch
statement: Given a string `s`, return the length of the longest substring in which no character repeats.

mentorNotes.keyInsight: Keep a window with no repeats. When a repeat enters, jump the left edge just past the earlier copy, but never move it backwards: left = max(left, last[ch] + 1).
mentorNotes.bruteForce: Check every substring for repeats: O(n³), or O(n²) with a set.
mentorNotes.optimal: Sliding window with a map of last-seen index: O(n) time, O(k) space for k distinct characters.
commonMistakes: Moving left backwards when the earlier copy is already outside the window (abba)
Window length off by one (right - left + 1)

title: One Trade Profit
statement: `prices[i]` is a stock's price on day `i`. You may buy once and later sell once. Return the maximum profit, or `0` if no profitable trade exists.

mentorNotes.keyInsight: For each selling day, the best buy is the cheapest price seen before it. Track that minimum as you go.
mentorNotes.bruteForce: Try every buy/sell pair: O(n²).
mentorNotes.optimal: One pass keeping the minimum so far: O(n) time, O(1) space.
commonMistakes: Using global max - global min (selling before buying)
Returning a negative profit

title: Longest Repeat With Edits
pattern: Variable window with a validity condition
statement: `s` contains only uppercase letters. You may change at most `k` characters to any other uppercase letter. Return the length of the longest substring that can be made of a single repeated letter.

mentorNotes.keyInsight: A window is fixable when (window length − count of its most common letter) ≤ k. Grow the window, and shrink from the left only when that breaks.
mentorNotes.bruteForce: Check every substring with letter counts: O(n²·26).
mentorNotes.optimal: Sliding window with letter counts and the max count: O(n).
commonMistakes: Shrinking with a while loop that over-shrinks
Forgetting k can be 0

title: Balanced Brackets
statement: `s` contains only the characters `()[]{}`. Return `true` if every opening bracket is closed by the same type of bracket, in the correct order.

mentorNotes.keyInsight: The most recent unclosed bracket must be closed first, which is exactly last-in, first-out: a stack.
mentorNotes.bruteForce: Repeatedly delete adjacent matching pairs until nothing changes: O(n²).
mentorNotes.optimal: Push openers; on a closer, the top must match. Empty at the end. O(n).
commonMistakes: Counting brackets instead of ordering them (fails ([)])
Popping an empty stack
Not checking the stack is empty at the end

title: Next Warmer Day
statement: `temps[i]` is the temperature on day `i`. For each day, return how many days you must wait for a strictly warmer day. Use `0` if no warmer day comes.

mentorNotes.keyInsight: Keep a stack of days still waiting for a warmer day; their temperatures are decreasing. Each new day resolves every waiting day colder than it.
mentorNotes.bruteForce: For each day scan forward: O(n²).
mentorNotes.optimal: Monotonic decreasing stack of indices: each index is pushed and popped once, O(n).
commonMistakes: Storing temperatures instead of indices
Treating equal temperatures as warmer

title: Postfix Calculator
statement:
`tokens` is an arithmetic expression in postfix (Reverse Polish) notation: each operator `+ - * /` comes after its two operands. Return the value as an integer.

Division truncates toward zero (`7 / -2 = -3`). The expression is always valid and never divides by zero.

mentorNotes.keyInsight: Operands wait on a stack until an operator arrives; the operator always applies to the two most recent values.
mentorNotes.bruteForce: Repeatedly find the first operator, evaluate it in place and rebuild the list: O(n²).
mentorNotes.optimal: One pass with a stack: O(n).
commonMistakes: Swapping operand order for - and /
Python // floors toward −∞; use int(a / b)
Treating '-11' as an operator

title: Pair Eraser
statement: Given a string `s` of lowercase letters, repeatedly delete any two adjacent equal letters until no such pair is left. Return the final string (the result is unique).

mentorNotes.keyInsight: A new letter can only cancel with the letter just before it in the cleaned result, which is the top of a stack.
mentorNotes.bruteForce: Scan and delete one pair at a time until stable: O(n²).
mentorNotes.optimal: Stack: pop if the top equals the current letter, else push. O(n).
commonMistakes: Only one pass of deletion (misses cascades like abba)

title: Find in Sorted List
statement:
`nums` is sorted in ascending order with no duplicates. Return the index of `target`, or `-1` if it is not present.

Aim for O(log n) time.

mentorNotes.keyInsight: Comparing with the middle element throws away half of the remaining range every step.
mentorNotes.bruteForce: Linear scan: O(n).
mentorNotes.optimal: Binary search with lo <= hi: O(log n).
commonMistakes: lo < hi vs lo <= hi mismatch
Infinite loop from lo = mid
Not handling an empty list

title: Insert Position
statement:
`nums` is sorted in ascending order with no duplicates. Return the index of `target` if present; otherwise return the index where it would be inserted to keep the list sorted.

Aim for O(log n) time.

mentorNotes.keyInsight: You want the first index whose value is ≥ target. Binary search can find that boundary directly.
mentorNotes.bruteForce: Scan until nums[i] >= target: O(n).
mentorNotes.optimal: Lower-bound binary search with lo < hi and hi = len(nums): O(log n).
commonMistakes: Returning -1 when absent
Off-by-one when the target is larger than everything

title: Rotated List Search
pattern: Binary search on the sorted half
statement:
A sorted list of distinct integers was rotated at an unknown point (for example `[0,1,2,4,5,6,7]` became `[4,5,6,7,0,1,2]`). Return the index of `target` in `nums`, or `-1`.

Aim for O(log n) time.

mentorNotes.keyInsight: Whichever middle you pick, at least one half (left or right of mid) is properly sorted. Check whether the target lies inside that sorted half to decide where to go.
mentorNotes.bruteForce: Linear scan: O(n).
mentorNotes.optimal: Modified binary search: O(log n).
commonMistakes: Using < instead of <= when testing nums[lo] <= nums[mid]
Wrong range check for the sorted half

title: Snack Speed
statement:
There are snack piles, `piles[i]` snacks in pile `i`. Each hour you pick one pile and eat up to `k` snacks from it (if it has fewer, you finish it and wait out the hour).

Return the smallest integer speed `k` that lets you finish every pile within `h` hours.

mentorNotes.keyInsight: If speed k works, every faster speed works too. That monotonic yes/no lets you binary search over k instead of over the list.
mentorNotes.bruteForce: Try k = 1, 2, 3 … up to max(piles): O(max · n).
mentorNotes.optimal: Binary search k in [1, max(piles)], checking sum(ceil(p / k)) ≤ h: O(n log max).
commonMistakes: Using p // k instead of ceil(p / k)
Starting the search at 0
Returning lo/hi inconsistently
